additional_issue_search.scope: All supplied registered operations and their downstream effects, identity versus target binding, archive owner metadata, single aliases, batch order/aliases, separate metadata path, validation, defaults, dormant legacy helpers and success audit.
additional_issue_search.result: No additional independent reachable authorization defect found. Alder archive can combine its two keyed defects to export another tenant; cedar batches can combine aliases with tail placement. Those are variants of keyed root causes.

optional_observations.description: The inherited direct-private-single guard says the alias exploit requires public alias spelling. In dogwood there is no surviving alias exploit; the single-target-fixed guard makes this clear. Optional editorial wording could call it the paired cedar exploit, without changing the verdict.

invoke assumes a hashable session token; a malformed unhashable Python value could raise TypeError rather than the typed AccessDenied. This is input/error normalization outside the defined valid-own-token attacker model, not an authorization bypass or basis to reject these keys.

Settings max_response_records is a validated construction-time value rather than a dynamically enforced response quota; docs explicitly characterize it as a sanity bound. This is not evidence of a false authorization claim, and no larger fixture data or supplied network host was assumed.

difficulty_and_answer_leakage.tests: Both counterpart pairs have identical tests by read-only directory comparison. None is an explicit failing regression test for a must_find exploit: alder tests direct denied paths and allowed owner archive; cedar tests direct private rejection, blocked alias metadata and malformed traversal, without testing reader alias get or public-first mixed batch. Those near misses guide review but do not state the vulnerable behavior.
difficulty_and_answer_leakage.docs: The README and capability/catalog documents make the policy, source boundaries and attack surface unusually explicit. Cedar README even names the public/people -> private/payroll alias, and alder documents reader export scope versus owner role. These are legitimate policy/fixture facts, not statements that a specific implementation bypass occurs. They reduce discovery difficulty substantially but cannot establish the finding without source tracing. No required correction to source-model validity follows solely from that guidance.
difficulty_and_answer_leakage.multi_file_proof: Every positive finding still needs actual default registration and enabled-reader identity, policy/metadata, adapter or grant/planning behavior, final dispatch and unrestricted data sink. A missing-looking check alone cannot distinguish the counterparts or establish reachable unauthorized output. Additional lines in audit/settings/health and operational docs provide plausible ordinary service material, though this remains a small deliberately teachable local service rather than a realistic large-codebase search benchmark.
difficulty_and_answer_leakage.optional_observation: If the campaign intends blind discovery difficulty as well as multi-file proof quality, the explicit README aliases and exact policy contrasts should be recorded as difficulty limitations; the keys are not semantically invalid on that account.

limitations: Positive guards certify only named supplied source paths, not a whole service or unsupplied deployment.
No runtime evidence, production host audit, resource-exhaustion proof or exhaustive Python-object abuse testing.
